findings.description: The fallback requires a slash for `**/`, although globstar must also match zero directory segments. Consequently, `**/*.md` still fails to exclude `.hidden.md`, and `fixtures/**/*.json` fails to exclude `fixtures/.hidden.json`. Native matching rejects these dot-files, so neither matcher handles them.
findings.failure_mode: Dot-files directly inside the glob's base directory remain reviewable despite matching the exclusion pattern, preserving the coverage-cap degradation this change is intended to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate a whole-segment `**/` into an optional directory prefix, allowing zero segments. Add regression tests for root dot-files and dot-files directly inside a named base directory.
findings.failure_scenario: Dot-files directly inside the glob's base directory remain reviewable despite matching the exclusion pattern, preserving the coverage-cap degradation this change is intended to fix.

findings.description: The retry is documented as dot-agnostic, but the translation `**` -> `.*` makes a leading `**/` require at least one `/` in the filename (`**/x` becomes `^.*/x$`). Native minimatch lets a leading `**` match zero segments, so for root-level paths the native matcher is the only one that can match, and it still applies the dot rule. Examples that remain unexcluded after this fix: `**/*.md` vs `.hidden.md`; `**/fixtures/**` vs `fixtures/.claude/settings.json`; `**/.claude/**` vs `.claude/.x/y`. The same applies to a trailing `/**` which cannot match the bare directory (`a/**` vs `a`), though that is not a file path in practice.
findings.failure_mode: A `.reviewignore` or `--exclude` pattern written with the common `**/` prefix still leaves root-level dot-led files in the review set, reproducing the bd-a8l0c symptom (file_cap pressure, incomplete_coverage) for that pattern shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate a leading `**/` to `(?:.*/)?` and a trailing `/**` to `(?:/.*)?` (and a bare `**` to `.*`) so the globstar can match zero segments, matching native semantics minus the dot rule. Add tests: `**/*.md` vs `.hidden.md` and `**/fixtures/**` vs `fixtures/.claude/x`.
findings.failure_scenario: A `.reviewignore` or `--exclude` pattern written with the common `**/` prefix still leaves root-level dot-led files in the review set, reproducing the bd-a8l0c symptom (file_cap pressure, incomplete_coverage) for that pattern shape.

findings.description: `pattern.split("**")` treats every `**` as a globstar regardless of position. Native `path.matchesGlob` (minimatch) only treats `**` as a globstar when it is a whole path segment; `**.md` or `src/**.ts` behave as `*.md` / `src/*.ts` (single segment). Because the new retry runs for every wildcard pattern the native matcher rejects, those patterns now match across `/` (`^.*\.md$` matches `docs/a/b.md`). This is a behaviour change unrelated to dot-led segments, which the brief said should not occur, and on a denylist it silently removes files from the review set.
findings.failure_mode: An operator pattern such as `**.md` (previously root-only) now excludes every markdown file at any depth with no diagnostic; coverage shrinks silently and reviewers may believe files were reviewed when they were excluded.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat `**` as a globstar when it is a full segment (`^\*\*$`, `^\*\*/`, `/\*\*/`, `/\*\*$`); otherwise collapse it to `*` (`[^/]*`), mirroring minimatch. Add a negative test: `**.md` does not match `a/b.md`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator pattern such as `**.md` (previously root-only) now excludes every markdown file at any depth with no diagnostic; coverage shrinks silently and reviewers may believe files were reviewed when they were excluded.

findings.description: The test `single * stays within one path segment` asserts `!matchesExcludePattern("evals/tests/fixtures/a/b.md", ["evals/tests/fixtures/*.md"])`. On the `hasNativeGlob === false` branch (Node without `path.matchesGlob`, i.e. < 20.17 / < 22.5) `simplifiedGlobMatch` handles a single-`*` pattern with `startsWith(before) && endsWith(after)`, which crosses `/` and returns true. The implementer's own report confirms this branch crosses segments. The new test therefore passes only on the native-glob branch and encodes a property `matchesExcludePattern` does not have on the fallback path.
findings.failure_mode: If any CI job or developer machine runs a Node version without `path.matchesGlob`, this test fails (`not ok - single * stays within one path segment`) even though the fix is correct for its target, blocking the suite for a pre-existing fallback quirk.
findings.suggested_fix: Either guard the assertion with the same `hasNativeGlob` condition (export it or test `typeof path.matchesGlob === 'function'`), or make the Node < 22 branch call `dotSegmentGlobMatch` for single-`*` patterns so both branches share segment semantics (the brief permits leaving the fallback alone, so the guard is the minimal option).
findings.failure_scenario: If any CI job or developer machine runs a Node version without `path.matchesGlob`, this test fails (`not ok - single * stays within one path segment`) even though the fix is correct for its target, blocking the suite for a pre-existing fallback quirk.

findings.description: `new RegExp(...)` is built on every call, i.e. once per (file, pattern) pair for every wildcard pattern the native matcher rejects, which on Node 22 is the common path for any file not matched. Additionally, each `**` becomes an unanchored `.*`, so a pattern with many `**` (e.g. `**a**a**a**a**a**a**a**`) compiles to a chain of `.*a` groups with polynomial backtracking against a non-matching filename. Patterns originate from `--exclude`, `exclude_patterns`, and `.reviewignore`; if `.reviewignore` is read from the PR head, a PR author controls them. Previously on Node 22 these patterns were handled only by minimatch, which does not build this regex shape.
findings.failure_mode: A pathological `.reviewignore` pattern can stall the review process for the whole file set (ReDoS), and ordinary large review sets pay repeated regex compilation cost that the triage's 100-file benchmark does not exercise.
findings.suggested_fix: Compile once per pattern (memoize `pattern -> RegExp` in a module-level Map or precompile before the file loop in `matchesExcludePattern`), collapse consecutive globstars so at most one `.*` is emitted per `**` run, and consider rejecting or truncating patterns with more than a small number of `**` segments.
findings.failure_scenario: A pathological `.reviewignore` pattern can stall the review process for the whole file set (ReDoS), and ordinary large review sets pay repeated regex compilation cost that the triage's 100-file benchmark does not exercise.

findings.description: The runtime entry point is `dist/main.js`, built from this source by `npm run build`. The diff changes `resources/core/truncation.ts` but contains no `dist/` or manifest changes, and the implementer report states `dist/` is untouched. The sprint plan requires the rebuild in the same commit and `tools/check-bb-dist-fresh.sh --check` to pass.
